'''Hans Bock''' (5 October 1928 – 21 January 2008) was a German chemist born in [[Hamburg]] and died in [[Königstein im Taunus]].

== Career ==
Hans Bock studied chemistry at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]], where he received his PhD in 1958 for his work on water-free [[hydrazine]] in the group of [[Egon Wiberg]].<ref name="nöth">Obituary (in German language) by [[Heinrich Nöth|H.Nöth]] [http://www.badw.de/publikationen/sonstige/nachrufe/2008/bock.pdf] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120311104703/http://www.badw.de/publikationen/sonstige/nachrufe/2008/bock.pdf |date=2012-03-11 }}</ref> In 1964, he received his postdoctoral lecture qualification after work on [[phosphorus]] containing [[Diazene|diacenes]] in the same research group. Subsequently, he had a three-year visit in the group of [[Edgar Heilbronner]] at [[ETH Zurich]] in Switzerland, where he worked on applications of the [[Hückel method|HMO-model]], leading to the textbook: ''The HMO model and its application''.

In 1968, he was announced full professor for inorganic chemistry at [[Goethe University Frankfurt]].<ref name="kaim">Obituary (in German language) by  [[Wolfgang Kaim|W.Kaim]]  [http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ange.200800607/pdf]</ref>

== Research ==
Bock is the author and co-author of more than 500 publications in peer-reviewed journals. His research focused on preparation of element-organic compounds and their characterisation by appropriate physical measurement methods. Main focus was set on development and application of [[X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy]] (XPS) for detection and characterisation of transient molecules.<ref name="herrmann">Obituary (in German language) by [[Wolfgang A. Herrmann|W.A.Herrmann]] [http://portal.mytum.de/archiv/reden_p/archive_folder.2008-02-14.7255149514]</ref>

He proposed the use of the [[super silyl group]] in 1993.

== Literature ==
* ''The HMO model and its application'' by Edgar Heilbronner and Hans Bock, translated by W. Martin and A. J. Rackstraw

== Recognition ==
He was an external member of [[Max-Planck-Gesellschaft]] and became adjunct professor at [[University of Michigan]] (Ann Arbor) and the [[Technical University of Munich]]. He received two honorary doctorates by the [[University of Hamburg]] and the [[University of Montpellier]] in France.

In 1987, he received the [[Wilhelm Klemm|Wilhelm-Klemm]]-Award<ref>[http://www.gdch.de/gdch/eps/preise/klemm.htm Wilhelm-Klemm-Award (in German language)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719031539/http://www.gdch.de/gdch/eps/preise/klemm.htm |date=2011-07-19 }}</ref> by the [[Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker]] (GDCh).
